_note: Yedek konu havuzu: Gemini bir senaryo uretemezse hat durmasin diye, ayrica yapimciya 'evergreen fikir' olarak veriliyor. Her konunun bir bicimi var: measured (rakamlar hikaye), story (belgelenmis bir olay, zaman sirasiyla), explain (bir yapay zeka davranisinin tek sasirtici nedeni), trend (gundem; yapimci canli sinyalden uretir). Hepsi DOGRULANABILIR: aritmetik ya da herkese acik bir belge. Hikayelerde ozel kisi/yasayan kisi adi yok; sirket, urun ve tarihi sistemler serbest. Konu secimi pipeline.backlog_candidates: son iki videoda kullanilmayan bicim one gecer.

topics.angle: A 60-second Short rendered in code costs $0. The same 60 seconds from the cheapest video model costs about $3.
topics.measure: published per-second price x 60

topics.angle: UTF-8 makes the same sentence cost different amounts in different alphabets. Latin 1 byte, accented 2, Japanese 3.
topics.measure: UTF-8 byte length of a parallel text
sources: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 1, parallel text

topics.angle: A model's context window is advertised in tokens, but what you can actually fit depends on the alphabet you write in.
topics.measure: characters per token across scripts

topics.angle: Output tokens usually cost several times more than input tokens, so a short answer to a long question is the cheap case.
topics.measure: input vs output price ratio across providers

topics.angle: Running a model locally is free per request but not free per hour: electricity plus hardware amortisation gives a real per-token cost.
topics.measure: GPU watts x local electricity price / tokens per second

topics.angle: Image generation is priced per image, video per second. At one frame per second the two prices stop matching.
topics.measure: price per image x 30 vs price per second of video

topics.angle: A speech model that runs on a laptop CPU is slower than real time; one that runs on a phone is not. The gap is smaller than the price gap.
topics.measure: real-time factor on CPU vs hosted price per minute

topics.angle: Free API tiers differ by three orders of magnitude in requests per day. The generous ones are not the ones with the famous names.
topics.measure: published free-tier request limits

topics.angle: Caching a prompt costs money to write and saves money to read. Below a certain reuse count it loses.
topics.measure: cache write price vs read saving, break-even reuse count

topics.angle: A thinking model that reasons for ten seconds bills those seconds as output tokens you never see.
topics.measure: reasoning token price x typical reasoning length

topics.angle: Embedding a million documents is cheaper than one hour of video generation, by a wide margin.
topics.measure: embedding price per million tokens vs video price per second

topics.angle: Open-weight models are free to download but the download itself is the smallest cost in using them.
topics.measure: model file size vs VRAM requirement vs rental price per hour

topics.angle: In 2016 Microsoft put a chatbot on Twitter that learned from the replies it received. It was taken offline in under a day.
topics.measure: timeline from launch to shutdown, as told in Microsoft's own post
topics.calc: launch, what users did, shutdown, what the company said afterwards
sources: Microsoft blog post 'Learning from Tay's introduction' (March 2016)
contemporary press coverage of the shutdown

topics.angle: An airline argued that its own chatbot was a separate entity responsible for what it said. The tribunal disagreed.
topics.measure: the sequence of the case: wrong answer, refused refund, argument, ruling
topics.calc: events in order, from the published decision
sources: British Columbia Civil Resolution Tribunal decision (February 2024)

topics.angle: In 1770 a chess machine beat nobles across Europe. It had a human hiding inside. Decades later a crowd-work marketplace borrowed its name.
topics.measure: timeline of the machine, from its debut to its exposure, and the later naming
topics.calc: debut, tours, how the hidden player worked, the later marketplace
sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica entry on the Turk chess automaton

topics.angle: A 1966 program only turned what you typed into a question, and people still told it their problems.
topics.measure: how the program worked, step by step, and how users reacted
topics.calc: one example exchange rebuilt from the published script, then the reaction

topics.angle: In 2023 a court filing cited legal cases that a chatbot had made up. The judge looked for them. None existed.
topics.measure: sequence from the filing to the court's order
topics.calc: filing, the opposing side's check, the judge's order, the outcome
sources: US District Court (S.D.N.Y.) order of June 2023
press coverage of the sanctions hearing

topics.angle: A language model never sees the letters in 'strawberry'. It sees a few chunks, which is why it can miscount them.
topics.measure: how a tokenizer splits the word, against counting the letters in code
topics.calc: token chunks of the word versus a letter count of the same word
sources: tokenizer documentation of a major model provider

topics.angle: A chatbot does not remember your chat. The app sends the whole conversation again with every message, and you pay for all of it.
topics.measure: input tokens billed per turn, summed over a ten-message chat
topics.calc: turn n re-sends turns 1 to n-1, so the total grows with the square of the length
sources: provider API documentation on conversation messages
provider pricing page for input tokens

topics.angle: A language model has no clock. It knows today's date only if the app writes it into the prompt.
topics.measure: what a bare API call contains versus what a chat app adds in front of it
topics.calc: a minimal request body versus the same request with a date line added
sources: provider API documentation on request structure
